After the separation of complementary strands of DNA during DNA replication, the separated strands of DNA can become twisted and coiled together to form tangles. The enzyme DNA topoisomerase II alpha (TOP2A) is able to remove these tangles in a two-step process: • step 1 – TOP2A forms a complex with the tangled DNA and catalyses the cleavage (cutting) of both strands to allow the strands to separate from one another • step 2 – TOP2A catalyses the repairs of the cuts made in the DNA so that the strands are complete.
